name: wc-design
description: A live, EDITABLE Claude Design canvas on the web-chat surface, seeded from the .dc.html working files in a directory you name and re-seeded by its host service whenever those files change, with ordinary web-chat comment pins anchored over the artboards - reach for it to look at, talk about and iterate on a design that already exists on disk, and to change it in place: the pane installs the editor's one-member host object before the canvas boots, so you get the real editing chrome (click-to-select with a quick menu, inline rich text, undo/redo, zoom) and a Save that writes your edits BACK into those same .dc.html files, routed through the seeding helper's own --extract over a loopback listener the service owns. The write discipline is the point: nothing under the directory is touched until that extract exits clean and returns at least one artboard, every replaced file is backed up into the build tree first, each write is write-then-rename with the whole batch rolled back on failure, canvas.json is compared by meaning rather than bytes, and it NEVER deletes - an artboard you remove inside the editor is reported as orphaned and its file left alone. Editing is a property of the SESSION, not of the files: it needs the host service running and trust-approved (`claude-web-chat trust design-canvas`), and isolate mode turns off the host object, saving and pins together. Pins land per artboard rather than per element. The pack ships none of Anthropic's code - the canvas editor is read at runtime from the copy Claude Code already wrote on this machine, so a machine that has never run /design has nothing to show.
